players.product: Automated test equipment (UltraFLEXplus, Photon 100 SiPho/CPO test, Omnyx board test) for AI compute

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Michelle Turner on Q2 segments: Semiconductor Test revenue was up $11 million from the first quarter and 128% from Q2 2025, split SoC $843 million, memory $212 million and IST $67 million. Compute remains the largest portion of SoC product revenue at 70%, with compute revenue up nearly 600% year-over-year on AI demand; the previously announced merchant GPU order shipped in the quarter. Auto and industrial strengthened, 'driven by power management demand increases for AI data center build-outs'; mobile grew seasonally by double digits quarter-over-quarter but 'remains below historical levels'. IST revenue was up 94% from the prior year on 'AI-related HDD storage demand from all three major suppliers in this space' (CEO: IST grew 2.5x quarter-over-quarter); CEO: given 'the strong forecast for greater than 20% annual exabyte growth and our design wins', he is confident IST grows over the midterm, with continued growth in the second half.
quarterly_data.figure: SoC $843M; memory $212M; IST $67M (+94% YoY); compute 70% of SoC product revenue, up nearly 600% YoY

quarterly_data.signal: Call P&L and cash detail. CEO Greg Smith: total revenue 'topped $1.3 billion, up over 100% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $2.47, up over 300% year-over-year'; CFO: sales up 4% sequentially. First half 2026: $2.6 billion revenue and $5.02 non-GAAP EPS, 'up close to 100% and 275% year-over-year respectively'. Gross margin 59.8%, 250 basis points above the prior year and down 110 basis points sequentially, 'driven in part by one-time benefits in the first quarter'; non-GAAP operating income $448 million, a 33.7% operating margin; OPEX rose on R&D and go-to-market investment for 2027 growth plus higher variable compensation. Free cash flow $378 million in the quarter and $579 million in the first half (up 150%); cash and investments $517 million; capital expenditures up $26 million from the prior quarter; working capital, predominantly inventory, increased 'in support of future sales'.
quarterly_data.figure: Non-GAAP EPS $2.47; H1 revenue $2.6B and non-GAAP EPS $5.02; GM 59.8%; non-GAAP operating income $448M (33.7%); FCF $378M

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Michelle Turner, Q3 2026 guidance: revenue $1.2 billion-$1.3 billion, non-GAAP EPS $1.85-$2.15, gross margin 58%-59% ('reflective of product mix and new product launches'), operating expenses about 29%-30% of sales and a non-GAAP operating profit rate of 28%-30%. 'Based on current customer order visibility', first-half revenue is now 50%-52% of annual revenue; the second-half outlook 'has strengthened' and the range was narrowed. Second half versus first half: growth in memory, auto and industrial, IST, Product Test and Robotics, offset by softness in mobile and order timing in compute. Q4 OPEX expected comparable to the Q3 guide; full-year gross margin 'Right around the 59%', just shy of the target earnings model; 'We remain confident in achieving our target earnings model at an accelerated pace', with an update at the Q4 call. CEO: 'We expect 2027 to be another year of healthy growth for Teradyne'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3: revenue $1.2B-$1.3B, non-GAAP EPS $1.85-$2.15, GM 58%-59%, operating profit rate 28%-30%; first half = 50%-52% of annual revenue

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Greg Smith on lead times and supply: 'our lead times are in the 16-week-ish range'. Bottlenecks through the AI supply chain, 'the supply of substrates for CoWoS, the supply of HBM memories, and basic advanced node fab capacity', have customers optimising their allocations, while 'all of the wafers that get fabbed are going to need to get tested'. Supply-disruption concern underpins the compute customers' dual-vendor strategy: 'They are working to qualify multiple test suppliers because they want to be sure that they're going to be able to get the capacity that they need when they need that capacity.'

CFO on Product Test and Robotics: Product Test revenue $107 million, up 26% year-over-year and 33% quarter-over-quarter, with growth across production board test, optical test, defense and aerospace and scale-up networking at the Multi-Lane Test Products (MLTP) JV; the new Omnics production board test platform had 'units already shipping in the second quarter', with continued growth expected in the second half. Robotics revenue $100 million, up 33% year-over-year and 9% quarter-over-quarter; electronics manufacturing and semiconductor revenue rose 50% from Q1 and is now the group's largest end market, which includes AI data centers; U.S. sales rose to 32% of Robotics sales and the U.S.-based manufacturing center is on track to open later this year. CEO: 'there is currently a multibillion-dollar market for assembly, automation, test, and burn-in equipment' at contract manufacturers and ODMs, 'and we expect mid-double-digit growth rates through the end of the decade'; Robotics is 'positioned to essentially grow in proportion with the rest of the company over this midterm', as the data-center build-out and reshoring push automation of assembly and test.
quarterly_data.figure: Product Test $107M (+26% YoY, +33% QoQ); Robotics $100M (+33% YoY, +9% QoQ); U.S. 32% of Robotics sales

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Greg Smith on the test-TAM framework and share: WFE capex approaching $250 billion by the end of the decade drives '5%-10% annual growth in 300-millimeter wafer production'. For 2027, test spending as a share of semi capex 'could revert down to 6%, 7% or so' ('It's possible') as WFE catches up, though he expects an increased TAM in 2027; fab-equipment money changes hands about a year before wafers come out, so 'It's three quarters on from when the revenue for the fab equipment has happened to when the revenue for the test equipment happens.' Share: 'our share in the compute segment is actually stabilizing and starting to inflect upward' in 2026, with the effect of share change visible in 2027 'but it's going to be gradual'. Networking: behind the physical layer is the switch silicon, where 'Teradyne has a terrific position in that market that we think will grow over the midterm independent of the physical layer'. Investment: leaning further into investments 'both organically and inorganically' and building out customer teams for major hyperscalers and semiconductor suppliers.
quarterly_data.figure: 300mm wafer production +5%-10% a year; test share of semi capex could revert to 6%-7% in 2027; fab-to-test revenue lag about three quarters

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Greg Smith on auto and industrial: 'I think it's likely 2027 is going to be up to or exceeding prior peaks in that space' ('my gut feeling'); the China power mix is about the same as at the prior peak, with some local competition. The Infineon deal is most helpful in wide bandgap discrete test, 'a smaller chunk of that market, but one that is expected to grow robustly', and positions Teradyne 'to establish a real leadership position in the testing of wide bandgap discretes'.

CEO Greg Smith on memory test: 'Our leadership position in HBM and DRAM maximizes our exposure to DRAM-driven growth.' In memory test, 'the part of the market where you test every bit is served by much lower priced, less differentiated equipment than the final test part of the market', so a big chunk follows bit growth and another part follows technology shifts; 'Our take is that the memory TAM is likely positioned for similar growth rates over the midterm that the SoC TAM is.'
